To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

people living in disadvantaged neighbourhoods are more likely to report adverse health effects and are less likely to adapt to heat, and that the most important factors associated with these two outcomes differ.
the characteristics of residents (including their adaptation index) and their buildings, as well as neighbourhood walkability, explain the prevalence of impacts and the adaptation index to heat.

the characteristics and perceptions of residents, dwellings and neighbourhoods are associated with the prevalence and adaptation to heat in the most disadvantaged areas of 9 large Canadian cities in 2011.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following question: What are the characteristics of people, dwellings and neighbourhoods that are associated with the self-reported adverse health impact of hot and humid conditions and the adaptation to it in disadvantaged sectors of the most populous cities in Québec, Canada?
the health impacts of climate change, particularly the impacts of heat waves on the health of the most disadvantaged people in cities.
understanding the relationship between the built environment and human health, with the goal of developing a theoretical model of the process of adaptation to heat.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the prevalence of impacts and the adaptation index are influenced by the individual, the building and the neighbourhood characteristics.
the more vulnerable the people, the more they rely on adaptation to cope with the heat.
the prevalence of impacts is associated to the adaptation index and to the individual characteristics, the building insulation and the walkability of the neighbourhood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
people living in disadvantaged neighbourhoods are more likely to suffer adverse health effects from heat and to be more reactive than preventive when it comes to adapting to it.
the more vulnerable you are, the less you adapt and the more you suffer from the heat.
the more vulnerable the people are to the heat, the more they adapt to it. The less vulnerable the people are, the more they are able to adapt
The main takeaway from our work is that
a better understanding of the process of exposure to heat, impacts, adaptation and vulnerability requires an analysis at multiple levels.
a better understanding of the determinants of adaptation to heat in vulnerable populations is needed to improve public health interventions.

the adaptation to heat is not only a matter of individual behaviour, but it depends on a combination of individual, building and neighbourhood factors, which are not always in the hands of the residents.
